newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Pizza Hut outlets closed in Rio de Janeiro state.
newsitem.headline: Pizza Hut outlets closed in Rio de Janeiro state.

text.p: The owners of the Pizza Hut franchise in Brazil's Rio de Janeiro state have closed down all the state's outlets because of low profitability, local O Globo newspaper said Saturday.
The Pena Branca group closed 18 branches in the state in a sudden move on April 4, the newspaper said.
According to Antenor Barros Leal, superintendent of the group, the restaurants saw profits of $20 million last year against $520 million for the whole group, the newspaper said.
The group, which intends to concentrate on its key chicken and wheat businesses, has been looking unsuccessfully for individual buyers for the outlets, it added.
Pena Branca group officials could not be immediately reached to comment on the report.
Pizza Hut is one of the restaurant operations of PepsiCo Inc. In January this year, PepsiCo announced it was spinning off its restaurant businesses to shareholders as an independently-traded company.
((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
